abstract: The best content marketing ideas for social media teach something useful, show how you work, prove your results, start a conversation and sometimes ask for the sale. Short video under 60 seconds is the format people say they interact with most on most networks. Use a steady mix, match it to the platform your customers use, and measure results that matter.

mainEntity.name: What are good content marketing ideas for social media?

acceptedAnswer.text: Teach with how-tos and answers to common questions, show behind-the-scenes work and your team, prove results with customer stories and reviews, start conversations with polls and live questions, and make clear offers now and then.

mainEntity.name: What is the most popular type of social media content?

acceptedAnswer.text: Short video under 60 seconds is the brand content people say they interact with most on TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and X in Sprout Social's 2026 survey. On LinkedIn, text posts lead.

mainEntity.name: How often should I post on social media?

acceptedAnswer.text: We found no reliable independent benchmark. Pick a rhythm you can keep for three months, such as three to five posts a week on your main platform, and put quality first.

mainEntity.name: What is a good mix of promotional and useful content?

acceptedAnswer.text: Give most posts to teaching and showing, and keep selling to a minority. This is a rule of thumb, not research. Adjust after a month of your own results.

mainEntity.name: Should I post the same content on every platform?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Keep the idea and change the format for each platform, for example a short video for Reels, a text post for LinkedIn and a carousel for both.

mainEntity.name: Should my business follow social media trends?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only when the trend fits your audience and tone, you can add something original, and the post will still make sense later. Skip trends tied to sensitive news.

mainEntity.name: How do I come up with content ideas consistently?

acceptedAnswer.text: Keep an idea bank fed by customer questions, comments, support tickets and your own analytics. Plan a month at a time and reuse each idea in several formats.

mainEntity.name: Do I have to label AI-generated content?

acceptedAnswer.text: Labeling is a good practice. In Sprout's Q1 2026 survey, unlabeled AI-generated content was what consumers most wished brands would stop doing. Check each platform's current rules.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to disclose sponsored posts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The FTC's Endorsement Guides say a material connection, such as payment or free products, must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously, in the same medium as the post.

mainEntity.name: How do I measure social media content?

acceptedAnswer.text: Judge each post by its job: saves and shares for teaching, replies for conversation, profile visits and clicks for proof, and clicks or sales for offers. Compare against your own recent average.

name: Glossary: Content Marketing Ideas for Social Media: 30 Ideas That Work

hasDefinedTerm.name: Carousel
hasDefinedTerm.description: A post made of several swipeable images or slides.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Reel or Short
hasDefinedTerm.description: A short vertical video format on Instagram, Facebook or YouTube.

hasDefinedTerm.name: User-generated content
hasDefinedTerm.description: Posts made by customers about your brand, shared with permission.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Material connection
hasDefinedTerm.description: A payment, free product or other link between a brand and a person who endorses it.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Content mix
hasDefinedTerm.description: The balance of post types you publish, such as teaching, showing, proving, joining and selling.
